Each warded creature also gains spell resistance 23 against spells cast by chaotic neutral, lawful neutral, neutral evil or neutral good creatures, and spell resistance 27 against spells cast by true neutral creatures, and is protected from possession and influence by such creatures as protection from evil. A chaotic neutral, lawful neutral, neutral evil or neutral good creature that hits a warded creature in melee is sickened for 1d6 rounds (Fortitude negates); a true neutral creature that does so is nauseated for 1d6 rounds (Fortitude negates) instead.

counterbalancing-aura.notes: The +4s apply against all attacks and effects, as the prose says explicitly, so they are emitted flat. The sickened and nauseated conditions are retributive — they land on the neutral creature that struck a warded creature, not on the warded creature — so they are narrated. Granted spell resistance has no home in the vocabulary.

effects.target: being flanked
The target sprouts extra eyes all over its body, including on the back of its head, gaining all-around vision.

countless-eyes.notes: Save is Will negates (harmless), so no save_gate. All-around vision is not one of the seven senses in the sense vocabulary, so it is narrated; the flanking immunity it confers does fit immunity, which takes free text.

effects.target: When a harmless spell of 3rd level or lower is cast by someone inside your 25-foot emanation, you may immediately gain that spell's benefit as though it had also targeted you.

The intended target still receives the spell in full. You only benefit if the caster is within the aura, and you count as the caster of your copy. If the copied effect could target creatures besides you, you cannot use it to help anyone else — the aura serves only you. Taking a spell this way ends the aura at once.

covetous-aura.notes: What it grants is whatever spell someone else happens to cast nearby, so nothing about the benefit is knowable here. 'Or until discharged' cannot be combined with the per-level term in the shared duration shape; the discharge is described in the narrative.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target is seized by insatiable greed and tries to steal any item worth 100 gp or more that it can see, each time it enters a new room or area, going for whichever it believes is worth most. The compulsion can push it into recklessness it would normally avoid — though never into something that would clearly kill it, badly harm it, or get it caught. In combat it must go after valuables it sees on an opponent, disarming for a valuable weapon or using the steal manoeuvre for something on a belt. Once it has either attempted a steal in combat or taken damage, the compulsion subsides until the current fight is over and it enters a new area. An affected target in combat that has neither tried to steal nor taken damage may attempt a save each round to shrug the spell off until the threat passes and it enters a new room. Break enchantment, limited wish, miracle, remove curse and wish each end it early; dispel magic does not touch it.

covetous-urge.notes: A behavioural compulsion with no condition or modifier attached. The 7 HD ceiling is already in the corpus targets line.

effects.target: AC, in any round the creature has not moved closer to an enemy or has moved at least 5 feet away from adjacent enemies
saving throws, in any round the creature has not moved closer to an enemy or has moved at least 5 feet away from adjacent enemies
attack rolls made as readied actions and attacks of opportunity, in any round the creature has not moved closer to an enemy or has moved at least 5 feet away from adjacent enemies
saving throws against fear effects

Alternatively, so long as it does not close with its enemies, the affected creature may instead raise the DC of all spells it casts as part of a readied action by 1. If it willingly moves toward a threatening creature the spell ends immediately.

coward-s-cowl.notes: Every bonus here is gated on the creature's movement that round, so all three are situational rather than a flat combat_mod or save_mod — a plain +1 AC would apply in rounds the spell explicitly withholds it. The +1 to attacks covers only readied actions and attacks of opportunity, never ordinary attacks. The fear penalty has no stated bonus type and is recorded untyped.

effects.target: Each round the target fails to attack you in melee it takes a further cumulative -1 penalty to Armor Class, attack rolls and saving throws, to a maximum of -5. At the end of each of its turns it may attempt a Will save to stop the penalty growing that round. All penalties reset to zero the moment it attacks you in melee, and start climbing again if it stops. They do not increase while the target is prevented from reaching you by physical restraint, magic or impassable terrain. If you move away from the target, the spell ends.

coward-s-lament.notes: Not emitted as combat_mod or save_mod specs: the penalty is zero on casting, grows by 1 each round the target does not engage you, caps at -5 and resets to zero whenever it does. A static -1 would be wrong on the first round and a static -5 wrong on every round but the fifth. The per-round Will save is likewise not a single save_gate.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: craft

crafter-s-curse.notes: The prose gives no type for the penalty, so it is recorded untyped rather than assigned one.

effects.target: craft
effects.note: the target's next Craft check only

crafter-s-fortune.notes: Save is Will negates (harmless), so no save_gate. The luck bonus type is stated in the prose. The spell lasts a day per level but discharges on the first Craft check, which the use limit carries; 'or until discharged' has no place alongside the per-level term in the shared duration shape.

effects.target: Creates one nonmagical weapon, shield or suit of armour. Make a Craft check against the item's normal creation DC; on a failure the item arrives with the broken condition. Including a scrap of a rare material as an extra component lets you make the item from it, but never cold iron.

create-armaments.notes: Creates an object. The broken condition applies to the item, not to a creature, and is not in the condition vocabulary.

effects.target: create lesser demiplane

As create lesser demiplane but up to ten 10-foot cubes per level, and it can expand a demiplane you already made rather than starting a new one (1 day/level). Cast inside your own demiplane it instead adds or removes one feature per casting, with an instantaneous duration: alignment trait (only an alignment you share), bountiful ecology feeding one Medium creature per 10-foot cube, an elemental-dominant trait, altered gravity, a seasonal and light cycle, a self-contained looping shape, or a linked physical structure such as a tree, castle, labyrinth or mountain. Permanency costs 20,000 gp, and each casting's area needs its own.

create-demiplane.notes: The duration line is 'days/level (1) or instantaneous (see text)' — which one applies depends on whether the casting expands the plane or edits a feature. The per-level term is emitted as the primary; the instantaneous alternative is in the narrative.

effects.target: create demiplane

As create demiplane but up to twenty 10-foot cubes per level, able to expand a plane made by either lesser version (1 day/level), and offering further features one per casting at instantaneous duration: a minor negative- or positive-dominant energy trait, a magic trait (dead, enhanced, impeded or wild — dead magic traps you inside unless the plane has a permanent portal), morphic control letting you use move earth at will at one tenth casting time and reshape plants likewise (rock at half time), a permanent two-way gate to a very familiar location on another plane, or an altered time trait (erratic, flowing at half or double rate, or timeless). Permanency costs 22,500 gp per casting's area.

create-demiplane-greater.notes: Same split duration as create demiplane; the per-level term is emitted and the instantaneous feature-editing mode narrated.

effects.target: Creates a small finite demiplane of up to three 10-foot cubes per level within the Astral or Ethereal Plane (your choice), filled with air or water, flat and featureless, at temperate spring conditions and a light level you set. It has no native life, counts as normal terrain for spells that shape earth, stone or wood, and you are 'very familiar' with all of it. On finishing the casting you may bring yourself and up to seven others there by joining hands. Others can only enter by planar travel magic. As a standard action you may eject a creature (Will negates); when the spell ends everyone is ejected with no save. It cannot be dispelled, but a creature inside can destroy it with limited wish, mage's disjunction, miracle or wish plus a successful dispel check. Recasting expands it or resets an area's duration; if one area expires, creatures there are shunted to the remaining parts, and sections cut off become separate demiplanes you control. Permanency costs 17,500 gp per area.

create-demiplane-lesser.notes: Planar creation. The ejection save is a use of the plane, made whenever you choose, not a gate on the casting, so no save_gate is emitted.

effects.target: Conjures one dose per three caster levels of aether, flayleaf, opium, pesh, scour, shiver or zerk. Doses must be used within 1 minute or they decay, though a drug taken before then runs its normal course. They cannot be sold but can be given away; a creature usually must be willing or helpless to take one, though some can be inhaled, applied to a wound, or slipped into food. The DC to resist a drug made this way is based on your caster level, not the drug's usual DC. A lawful evil worshipper of Mahathallah may instead create adyton, once per week regardless of level or castings.

create-drug.notes: Each of the seven drugs has its own ability damage, effects and addiction rules, none of them restated here, and which drug is made is chosen at casting — so nothing numeric could be emitted. The 1-minute duration is the shelf life of the doses, not the length of the drug's effect.

effects.target: Creates simple, nourishing, bland food and clean water enough to sustain three humans or one horse per caster level for 24 hours. The food decays and becomes inedible after 24 hours, though purify food and water keeps it fresh another 24; the water does not spoil.

create-food-and-water.notes: Creates provisions. The 24 hours is how long the food lasts.

effects.target: create undead

As create undead, except that it raises more powerful and intelligent undead from the corpse, fixed by caster level: shadow at 15th or lower, wraith at 16th-17th, spectre at 18th-19th, devourer at 20th or higher.

create-greater-undead.notes: Creates an NPC. What the resulting undead can do belongs to its stat block, not to this spell.

effects.target: Creates a path of paired handholds about 3 feet apart on earthen, plaster, stone or wooden walls — never metal or harder material — following the path you gesture out while casting. The path runs up to 30 feet from you plus 10 feet per 3 caster levels, maximum 90 feet at 18th level. Each hold juts about 6 inches out and is 10 inches long, well shaped for fingers or claws. When the spell ends, anything the handholds were supporting immediately falls.

create-holds.notes: Terrain creation. The prose sets no Climb DC for the holds, so none is invented.

effects.target: You and one creature enter an immersive mindscape you build: overt or veiled, harmless or harmful, any shape, size and gravity trait short of harmful gravity, with normal time, normal magic and no alignment traits. You place both arrivals and need no line of sight, only awareness of the target within range — though among unseen creatures the subject is picked at random, and among creatures you have seen firsthand you choose unerringly. You must appear inside it, and must build in an exit that is genuinely achievable, however obscure. Everyone inside can take no actions in the real world and their bodies lose their Dexterity bonus to AC. You may run illusory creatures there but only one is believable at a time; the rest stay silent or repeat generic phrases. In a veiled mindscape a creature gets a Will save the first time it interacts with the environment: disbelieving tells it where it is and how to leave, but it must still travel there to get out. In an overt mindscape it simply knows the way out. The spell ends when you leave, freeing everyone; anyone dropping below 0 hit points inside returns to its body, and if that is you the spell ends. Permanency by a 12th-level caster costs 10,000 gp, after which mindscape door lets people come and go.

create-mindscape.notes: The Will save is to disbelieve, and even a success leaves the creature inside the mindscape — it is not a negation — so no save_gate is emitted around the effect. Losing your Dexterity bonus to AC is narrated rather than converted to flat-footed: flat-footed also forbids attacks of opportunity, which this prose never says.

effects.target: create mindscape

As create mindscape, except that it takes one creature per caster level, lasts days rather than minutes, lets you choose the mindscape's magic trait, and lets you direct a number of believable illusory creatures at once equal to your caster level. Permanency by a 15th-level caster costs 17,500 gp.

create-mindscape-greater.notes: Same disbelief structure as create mindscape.

effects.target: ref

on_failure.target: The creature falls into the pit and takes falling damage as normal for the depth.

effects.note: Creatures standing where the pit is conjured save at the listed DC; a creature that ends its turn in a square adjacent to the pit saves with a +2 bonus. A creature pushed in by a bull rush or similar effect gets no save at all.

effects.target: Creates a 10-foot-square extradimensional hole 10 feet deep per 2 caster levels, maximum 30 feet, on any horizontal surface large enough — a ship's deck as readily as a dungeon floor. It has no weight and does not displace the material beneath. The sloped edges catch creatures ending their turn beside it. The coarse stone walls have a Climb DC of 25. When the spell ends, anyone inside rises with the pit's floor to stand on the surface over one round.

create-pit.notes: Falling damage is not emitted as a damage spec: the prose says 'as normal', giving no dice, and the amount depends on the pit's depth, which depends on caster level. The duration line is '1 round + 1 round/level'; the shared shape has no compound form, so the per-level term is emitted and the extra round recorded here.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: dead
on_failure.note: a living (dying) target dies as its soul is drawn into the gem; a target already dead simply loses its soul to the gem

effects.target: You draw the ebbing life force of a dying creature, or one dead within the past round, through a crystal lens into a soul gem whose value depends on the creature. A creature already dead still resists with a Will save as if alive. Only one gem can be made from a given creature. The gem crumbles when the spell ends, releasing the soul to judgement. Resurrecting a body whose soul is in a gem requires a caster level check against this spell's save DC — failure means the resurrection does nothing, success shatters the gem and the creature returns to life normally — and the DC of that check rises by 2 if the gem sits in an unholy location such as an unhallow. A souldrinker may expend 5 soul points when casting to fill the gem with the equivalent of one basic soul.

create-soul-gem.notes: The dead condition is emitted because the prose states it plainly, of the spell's own single target, at the moment of casting. The corpus already restricts the target to a dying or recently dead creature, so this cannot kill a healthy one.

effects.target: Cut a fairly flat piece — hide, carapace, skin — from a creature dead no more than 24 hours and with a physical body, and it becomes a map of the valuables that creature knew of in life, revealing one source of treasure per three caster levels. You pick the scale at creation: nearby (a dungeon level or two), local (a valley or community), or broad (a country or larger). It is accurate only to what the creature believed at death, faults and all, and knows nothing of changes since. What it marks is what that creature valued, which might be good food, suitable mates, or your own vault.

create-treasure-map.notes: Divination that produces an object; the contents are the GM's to place.

effects.target: Infuses a corpse with negative energy to raise a more powerful undead than animate dead can: ghoul at caster level 11th or lower, ghast at 12th-14th, mummy at 15th-17th, mohrg at 18th or higher. You may deliberately raise something weaker than your level allows. The undead is not automatically yours — if you can command undead, you may attempt to command it as it forms. Must be cast at night.

create-undead.notes: Creates an NPC; its abilities belong to its stat block.

effects.target: create undead
As create undead, except that from a corpse steeped at least 24 hours in a peat bog it raises one of three variant mummies: a bog mummy, an ice mummy, or an Osirian tomb guardian.

create-variant-mummy.notes: Creates an NPC; its abilities belong to its stat block.

effects.target: Creates up to 2 gallons of clean drinkable water per caster level, either filling a space just large enough to hold it or spread over three times that area — a downpour, or many small vessels filled at once. Unconsumed water vanishes after a day. Conjuration cannot create it inside a creature. Water weighs about 8 pounds per gallon; a cubic foot is roughly 8 gallons and 60 pounds.

Sheets a calm horizontal surface — floor, ground, a placid lake, a gentle river — with hard opaque ice 1 inch thick per caster level, up to one 10-foot square per level. It cannot form where objects or creatures already stand and must be smooth and unbroken when made. It bears a horse's weight, so creatures can cross water on it. Each 10-foot square has 3 hit points per inch of thickness and is hit automatically; a square reduced to 0 becomes chunks, slush and snow that count as difficult terrain. Breaking through with one attack instead needs a Strength check against DC 15 + your caster level. Each round on your turn the sheet grows 1 foot in every direction except toward you — slowly enough for anyone to step clear. A creature whose square the ice fully covers must choose to move onto the ice, be knocked prone on it, or be bull rushed into an adjacent square.

creeping-ice.notes: The Reflex save is not emitted as a save_gate: it belongs to the ice's growth on later rounds, not to the casting, and the prose gives the caught creature a three-way choice rather than a fixed outcome. The spell deals no damage at all despite the cold descriptor, so no damage spec belongs here.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: crime wave
A sudden criminal impulse takes the target, compelling it to commit a criminal act exactly as though it were under crime wave — roll on that spell's behaviour table.

crime-of-opportunity.notes: The whole substance is crime wave's, applied to one creature for one round.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Roll d% each round for each affected creature. 1-25: act normally but suspiciously — no benefit from or to teamwork feats or aid another, and a 50% chance of resisting any harmless spell or effect aimed at it (taking an attack of opportunity against the caster, forcing an attack roll for a touch spell, or making a save). 26-50: attempt a steal manoeuvre or Sleight of Hand check to take a random valuable from the nearest creature, or a nearby obviously valuable unattended object, moving adjacent as needed; once it has stolen something, later results of 26-50 make it flee with the loot and fight to keep it. 51-75: break, destroy or deface the nearest unattended manufactured object or structure, or merely vandalise it if it is too tough to damage. 76-100: attack the nearest creature (a familiar counts as part of itself). A creature that cannot carry out its result moves to the nearest cover or concealment and attempts a Stealth check to hide — or turns invisible instead, if it can.

crime-wave.notes: A per-round random behaviour table, rerolled every round; nothing on it is a fixed effect this spell inflicts.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target is affected by a dose of breath of the mantis god. The poison's Fortitude DC is this spell's DC rather than the poison's usual one.

effects.note: Only after the ranged touch attack hits.

effects.target: Your salivary glands fill with venom; make a ranged touch attack against one target in range to spit it.

crimson-breath.notes: The poison's damage, frequency and cure are breath of the mantis god's and are not restated here, so nothing numeric could be emitted. The one number the prose does give — the save DC — is the spell's own, which the save_gate already carries.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The toucher's skin turns bright red for 1 hour per caster level. The colour cannot be washed off, though it can be dispelled.

effects.note: Triggered whenever a creature other than you touches the warded object or area.

effects.target: Wards an object or up to a square foot of area with your personal rune, visible or invisible as you choose, harming the material not at all. Detect magic makes an invisible mark glow; see invisibility, true seeing, a gem of seeing or a robe of eyes also reveal it, and read magic reads any words. The ward itself cannot be dispelled but you or an erase spell can remove it.

crimson-confession.notes: The duration line reads 'permanent and hours/level (1)': the ward is permanent, and 1 hour/level is how long the red skin lasts on someone who triggers it. The permanent term is emitted for the spell and the hourly term left on the effect it triggers, since the shared shape cannot hold both.

effects.target: cha

A 120-foot emanation compels every creature of fewer than 8 HD to stop and attend to you; such a creature that wants to act against you must make a Will save first, and one that fails on its first attempt at a hostile action is enthralled, as the enthrall spell, for the duration so long as it stays in the area, and will not leave of its own accord. Creatures of 8 HD or more are unaffected. Everyone who hears you speak understands you telepathically, and you may make up to three suggestions to creatures of fewer than 8 HD in range as though using mass suggestion (Will negates), binding only those in range when each suggestion is made.

crown-of-glory.notes: The +4 Charisma is emitted plainly: this is a personal spell, the bonus is yours, and the enhancement type is stated. Everything else is gated on the listener having fewer than 8 HD, which no spec can test, so it is narrated rather than applied to whoever stands in the area.

effects.target: Once per round as a standard action, teleport to a creature suffering a fear effect within medium range that you are aware of, carrying objects up to your maximum load.

You detect fear as sense fear, but out to medium range. You arrive in a random open space within 20 feet of the creature and immediately resume sensing feared creatures from there. Having teleported, you can take no further actions that round, as with dimension door. If no creature in range is suffering a fear effect, you cannot teleport at all.

cruel-jaunt.notes: Detecting fear is not one of the seven entries in the sense vocabulary, so it is narrated alongside the teleport permission.

effects.target: The touched melee weapon gains the bane weapon quality against evil outsiders. On a confirmed critical hit against an outsider with the evil subtype it deals normal critical damage and also leaves that outsider nauseated for 1d3 rounds; a successful Fortitude save reduces this to sickened for 1 round.

crusader-s-edge.notes: The nauseated condition is not emitted as an apply_condition: it lands on an evil outsider you critically hit later, not on the spell's target, which is the weapon. Bane is a weapon quality — a +2 effective enhancement and +2d6 damage against the favoured type — but this prose names neither number, so nothing is emitted for it.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: attack
damage
fort
ref
will
The same -2 penalty also applies to all ability checks and all skill checks.

effects.target: Crushing despair counters and dispels good hope.

crushing-despair.notes: The -2 to weapon damage is emitted as a combat_mod because this is a debuff landing on the creatures in the cone — it lowers the damage of whoever it is applied to, which is the intended victim. The blanket penalty to ability and skill checks is narrated: skill_mod takes one named skill from the vocabulary and there is no 'all skills' target. No bonus type is stated in the prose, so all five are recorded untyped.

effects.target: Diplomacy checks to influence members of the culture you adapted to (does not stack with a circumstance bonus you already have from actually belonging to that culture)
Disguise checks to pass yourself off as a member of that culture
the DC of enchantment (charm) spells you cast against natives of that culture

Choose a culture or subculture at casting. If you already speak its native language you speak it with a native accent — the spell teaches you no language, but combines with tongues. Your body language, gestures and small unconscious choices mark you as a native. The Disguise bonus gives nothing toward impersonating a specific person, but it does cancel any circumstance penalty for not behaving appropriately to that person's culture.

cultural-adaptation.notes: Both +2s are scoped to one culture chosen at casting, so they are situational rather than flat skill_mods on Diplomacy and Disguise. The +1 raises the DC of spells you cast rather than modifying anything on your own sheet, and the prose gives it no type.

effects.target: Diplomacy checks to influence members of the culture you adapted to
Disguise checks to pass yourself off as a member of that culture
the DC of enchantment (charm) spells you cast against natives of that culture

Choose a culture at casting. If you already speak its native language you speak it with a native accent — the spell teaches no language but combines with tongues. Your body language, gestures and small unconscious choices mark you as a native.

cultural-adaptation-taldan.notes: This Taldan variant words the Diplomacy bonus as a bare '+2' with no type, where the general cultural adaptation calls its equivalent a circumstance bonus. The two are recorded as the prose writes them rather than levelled with each other — the Diplomacy bonus here is untyped, the Disguise bonus circumstance.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The target begins to dehydrate under the normal thirst rules, and no amount of drinking counters it — though any liquid it drinks still has its other effects, such as a poison or a potion. The nonlethal damage from this spell can never exceed the target's hit points. Break enchantment, limited wish, miracle, remove curse or wish removes the curse, but damage already suffered from dehydration must be healed normally.

cup-of-dust.notes: The dehydration damage comes from the thirst rules, not from this prose, which gives no dice and no interval — only a cap. Emitting a damage spec would mean inventing both the amount and the frequency.

effects.note: scales with caster level

effects.target: The target also gains the benefits of the material component in full. Roll this spell's healing separately from the component's when totalling hit points restored.

curative-distillation.notes: Healing, not damage: the prose says 'restores a number of hit points'. Save is Will half (harmless), so no save_gate wraps it. Scaling matches the shape the corpus already uses for the cure line.

effects.note: scales with caster level

effects.target: As with other cure spells, this deals that amount as damage to undead in the area instead of healing them, and each affected undead may attempt a Will save for half.

cure-light-wounds-mass.notes: The undead reversal is narrated, not emitted as a damage spec. It is conditional on the target being undead, which no spec can test, and this spell is aimed at one creature per level chosen by the caster — a damage spec here would hurt the living allies the casting is meant to heal. This is the same trap in reverse that made blaze of glory read as damage.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The object becomes flawed and prone to failure, according to what it is. Magic item: it functions intermittently, gaining either an unreliable curse or a random dependent curse. Nonmagical armour or shield: it gains the fragile armour quality. Nonmagical weapon: it gains the fragile weapon quality. Tool: it gains the broken condition whenever a creature rolls a natural 1 on a skill check with it. Anything else: 5% chance per day of use of gaining the broken condition. Artifacts are unaffected. The bearer is not compelled to keep the item and may sell or discard it. A cleric of Groetus using an affected item may make a DC 20 Will save to override the curse for 1 day.

effects.note: Will negates (object).

curse-item.notes: Every outcome lands on an object and depends on which kind of object it is. Broken is an item condition, not one of the creature conditions in the vocabulary.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: bestow curse
As bestow curse, except that the DC to remove the curse equals this spell's save DC + 5.

curse-major.notes: Which of bestow curse's penalty options applies is the caster's choice at casting and this prose restates none of them, so the spell_effect spec points at bestow curse rather than duplicating a number.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target can no longer receive luck bonuses, nor benefit from anything letting it roll twice and take the higher result (a swashbuckler's charmed life), nor choose a die result instead of rolling (taking 10 or 20, or a bard's lore master). On top of that, the first time each turn it would succeed at an attack, a saving throw or a skill check, it must roll twice and take the worse result. The curse cannot be dispelled, only removed by break enchantment, limited wish, miracle, remove curse or wish.

curse-of-befouled-fortune.notes: Shutting off a whole category of bonus, and forcing a reroll-take-worse, are changes to how dice are resolved rather than modifiers of any size. Nothing in the vocabulary can suppress luck bonuses or alter a roll's resolution.

effects.target: will

on_failure.note: fires 1 hour after the target next falls asleep, NOT at casting; scales with caster level

on_failure.target: The target also catches fire, taking 2d6 fire damage at the end of its turn each round until it dies or the flames are quenched normally. If it was still asleep, this damage wakes it.

curse-of-burning-sleep.notes: The 1d6 per 2 levels is emitted: it is dealt to this spell's own single target, in a stated amount, once. What the shape cannot carry is WHEN — it triggers an hour after the target next sleeps, not at casting — so that is written onto the spec's note and the duration is until_discharged to mark it as a triggered effect. The 2d6 catching-fire damage is deliberately left narrative because it repeats every round until death or quenching, and the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type. The spell does nothing at all to creatures that do not sleep. The fire element is already derived in the corpus.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: You name a trigger at casting — a kind of creature, object or condition, such as beggars, filthy clothing, diseased creatures, the king, blood, spiders, rats, corpses or sewage. Whenever the target comes within 30 feet of that trigger and is aware of it, it becomes sickened and feels a compulsion to leave. A successful Will save cancels the urge to leave but not the sickened condition, which lasts as long as it stays within 30 feet and aware.

curse-of-disgust.notes: The sickened condition is NOT emitted as an apply_condition. The curse is permanent but the sickening is not — it applies only while the target is within 30 feet of a trigger it can perceive. An apply_condition here would leave the target permanently sickened, which is far worse than the spell actually does.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: If the target ever tries to fly more than 5 feet above the ground, paper insects erupt around it and foul its movement: its flight manoeuvrability drops one step for every 3 of your caster levels. A creature pushed below clumsy manoeuvrability must land at the end of each of its turns or fall. Incorporeal or otherwise intangible creatures, including a wizard flying by gaseous form, are unaffected.

curse-of-dragonflies.notes: Manoeuvrability steps are not a speed number, and the speed spec takes a signed distance — the target's fly speed is untouched. Nothing here can be emitted without inventing a figure the prose never gives.

effects.target: Touching the ground curses a 2-mile radius with drastically changed weather, as the unseasonable weather curse. The focus merges into the cursed area during casting and can only be recovered if the curse is lifted.

curse-of-fell-seasons.notes: The substance is the unseasonable weather curse's, which this prose does not restate, and it is a curse entry rather than a spell — so no spell_effect spec is emitted pointing at something the corpus does not hold.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target cannot sell, trade, drop or give away any possession other than ordinary currency. It may buy things with coin but can never resell what it buys, and it may accept gifts but can offer nothing in return. Break enchantment, limited wish, remove curse, miracle or wish ends it; dispel magic does not touch it.

curse-of-keeping.notes: A restriction on what the target may do with its property — the inverse of a permission, which the vocabulary has no term for.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target gains the negated spellblight for the duration. Dispel checks made to remove that spellblight take a -5 penalty because of this spell's interference.

curse-of-magic-negation.notes: The negated spellblight's own effects are defined elsewhere and not restated here. The -5 falls on whoever later tries to dispel the blight, a third party, so it is not emitted as a modifier.

effects.target: Touching the ground curses a 1-mile radius to remain in bleak darkness, as the endless night curse. The focus merges into the cursed area during casting and can only be recovered if the curse is lifted.

curse-of-night.notes: The substance is the endless night curse's, which this prose does not restate and which is a curse entry rather than a spell in the corpus.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: Everything about the target grates, and everyone reads the worst into him. He must roll twice and take the lower result on every Bluff, Diplomacy, Intimidate and Perform check, and every creature he meets has its initial attitude toward him worsened by one step — helpful to friendly, friendly to indifferent, and so on.

curse-of-the-outcast.notes: Roll-twice-take-lower is not a fixed penalty, so no skill_mod could express it without inventing a number; attitude steps have no home in the vocabulary either.

effects.target: curse terrain, lesser
As lesser curse terrain, except that touching the ground curses a 1-mile radius with four unnatural hazards, using the effects of the major perilous demesne curse.

curse-terrain.notes: The hazards belong to the major perilous demesne curse, a curse entry rather than a spell, and are not restated here.

effects.target: curse terrain, lesser
As lesser curse terrain, except that touching the ground curses a 5-mile radius with six unnatural hazards, using the effects of the greater perilous demesne curse.

curse-terrain-greater.notes: Same structure as curse terrain; the hazards belong to the referenced curse entry.

effects.target: Touching the ground curses a 300-foot radius with three unnatural hazards, as the minor perilous demesne curse. The hazards appear frequently but unpredictably — you control neither when they start or stop nor where in the cursed terrain they appear. Curse terrain spells can be made permanent with permanency and stay dismissible afterwards: lesser at caster level 9 for 2,500 gp, curse terrain at 11 for 7,500 gp, greater at 15 for 17,500 gp, supreme at 19 for 27,500 gp.

curse-terrain-lesser.notes: The hazards themselves are the minor perilous demesne curse's and are not restated here, so nothing numeric could be emitted.

effects.target: curse terrain, lesser
As lesser curse terrain, except that touching the ground curses a 5-mile radius with seven unnatural hazards, using the effects of the grand perilous demesne curse.

curse-terrain-supreme.notes: Same structure as curse terrain; the hazards belong to the referenced curse entry.

effects.target: Imbues a touched 1-pint flask of water with negative energy, turning it into unholy water. Unholy water damages good outsiders the way holy water damages undead and evil outsiders.

curse-water.notes: Creates an item. The damage unholy water later does is the flask's when thrown, at whoever it is thrown at — not this spell's, and this prose gives no dice for it, so no damage spec is emitted.

effects.target: Touching the ground blights a 1-mile radius with one effect of your choice. Famine: all normal plants there halve their growth and food production, as the stunt growth effect of diminish plants. Living Death: any creature of Small size or larger killed in the area, and any corpse buried there, rises as an uncontrolled zombie 24 hours after death — burning or dismembering the corpse prevents this. Plague: every day at sundown every creature in the area must make a Fortitude save or immediately contract a disease you chose at casting, with no onset period — blinding sickness, bubonic plague, cackle fever, filth fever, leprosy, mindfire, red ache, shakes or slimy doom — thereafter using that disease's own frequency and DC. This is a disease effect.

cursed-earth.notes: Which of the three effects applies is chosen at casting, and only one involves a save. That save repeats daily for everyone in a 1-mile radius rather than gating the casting, and the disease that follows has numbers this prose never states.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: bestow curse
The creature suffers the curse option you chose at casting, from any option available with bestow curse.

effects.note: The save is made by the next creature to take the treasure or remove items from the container, not at casting; spell resistance applies.

effects.target: You curse an unattended piece of treasure, or a container of treasure, with any option available to bestow curse. The next creature to take the treasure or pull items from the container is cursed. If that creature turns out to be you, the spell instead discharges harmlessly.

cursed-treasure.notes: Which curse option applies is the caster's choice from bestow curse's list and is not restated here, so spell_effect points at bestow curse rather than duplicating a number. Like curse of burning sleep, the effect fires on a trigger rather than at casting; that timing is written onto the gate's note because the shape cannot carry it, and until_discharged marks it.

effects.target: Invisible bands of force ring the target's vital areas without hindering movement, halving damage from constriction, falling, being buried and similar crushing effects such as crushing hand. Grapple checks for anything other than constricting — pinning, swallowing whole — are unaffected. Once the bands have blocked 12 points of damage per caster level, to a maximum of 120 at 10th level, the spell discharges. They do nothing against incorporeal attacks unless those deal constriction or crushing damage, or would themselves be subject to damage reduction.

cushioning-bands.notes: DR 2/piercing or slashing fits damage_reduction exactly, with the bypass field naming what cuts through it. Halving crushing damage is a multiplier rather than a flat reduction and has no spec, and the 12-per-level absorption pool has no home either — the use limits count uses, not points absorbed. Save is Will negates (harmless), so no save_gate. The force element is already derived in the corpus.
